claims.text: Introducing a sintering aid can reduce the sintering temperature of ceramic materials.
Sintering aids reduce sintering temperature by promoting liquid-phase formation at ceramic grain boundaries.
The proposed intervention is adding a small amount of an oxide or glassy sintering aid to ceramic powder before sintering.
The proposed processing conditions use a controlled atmosphere, standard heating rates, and ambient pressure.
The sintering aid forms a transient liquid phase at grain boundaries.
A transient grain-boundary liquid facilitates particle rearrangement.
A transient grain-boundary liquid facilitates particle bonding.
The sintering aid produces a localized liquid phase at a lower temperature than would otherwise be available.
The localized liquid phase enhances diffusion.
The localized liquid phase increases particle contact.
Enhanced diffusion and particle contact reduce the temperature required for densification.
Aid-containing samples will attain densification comparable to additive-free samples at a lower sintering temperature.
Aid-containing samples will attain grain growth comparable to additive-free samples at a lower sintering temperature.
Conventional solid-state sintering of pure ceramic powder requires a higher temperature to achieve comparable densification.
The method is expected to apply only when the aid can form an effective liquid phase without degrading final material properties.
The method may be ineffective in ceramic systems that do not support transient liquid formation.
Additive incorporation may adversely alter the ceramic microstructure.
